title: Stronger leaf and split regularization in XGBoost
spec: Keep the L1 XGBoost residual model but regularize the trees explicitly. Set reg_lambda=10 (L2 penalty on leaf weights), gamma=1.0 (minimum loss reduction per split), max_depth=4, min_child_weight=5, learning_rate=0.03 and n_estimators=900. Keep subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3, and seed everything with random_state=seed. The goal is to test whether a smoother, shallower ensemble generalizes better across unseen scaffolds than the current deeper, lightly regularized trees.

title: Scaffold-bagged XGBoost ensemble with median aggregation
spec: Inside fit_predict, train B=8 XGBoost L1 models. Each one uses a bootstrap sample of the training molecules drawn by sampling unique Murcko scaffold groups with replacement (use rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold on the training SMILES), so the bags follow the scaffold structure that the harness uses. Give each model its own seed derived from the seed argument. Predict the test molecules with each model and return the element-wise median across the B predictions. The median suits MAE and the bags reduce variance. Keep the per-model XGBoost settings but use n_estimators=400 to stay within the time limit.

title: Applicability-domain similarity-density features
spec: Compute Morgan bit-vector Tanimoto similarity between every molecule and the training set. For each molecule, append three features: the mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training neighbours, the maximum similarity, and the mean target of those 5 neighbours. For training molecules, compute these out of fold with a 5-fold split, excluding the molecule itself and any molecule from its own fold, so the features are not leaked. Append the three columns to the XGBoost residual matrix. These features tell the booster how far a test molecule is from the training distribution, where the Murcko-scaffold split makes errors largest.

title: Spline-expanded physchem base
spec: In fit_predict, replace the Ridge physchem base with a pipeline of StandardScaler, then sklearn SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3, extrapolation='linear') applied to the 7 physchem features, then Ridge(alpha=3.0). Fit it on train physchem features and predict test as before. The residual XGBoost stages stay the same and consume base_tr and base_te. Splines give each physchem feature a smooth nonlinear shape without the explosion of pairwise terms seen with degree-2 polynomials.

title: Scaffold-holdout robust weighting of the physchem base
spec: Make the physchem base robust to scaffold clusters. Compute Murcko scaffolds of the training molecules and group them. Fit the Ridge base with sample weights 1/sqrt(size of the molecule's scaffold group), so that large scaffold families do not dominate the linear fit. Normalize the weights to mean 1. Then fit the XGBoost L1 residual model unchanged on the residual target. The aim is to make the linear trend follow the many distinct chemotypes rather than the few heavily represented ones.

title: Gain-based descriptor selection
spec: Fit a quick XGBoost squared-error model (100 rounds, max_depth=4, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed) on the full featurized matrix. Keep only the top 60 RDKit descriptor columns by total gain plus all 2048 Morgan count columns, dropping the rest, and use this reduced matrix for both residual XGBoost stages. The selection uses only training labels, so it is valid inside fit_predict. The aim is to reduce the noise from weak descriptors that dilute column sampling, which is the dominant regularizer here.

title: Column-weighted sampling that favours physchem features
spec: Keep the current two-stage XGBoost model, but pass feature_weights to XGBoost's fit for both stages. Give the 6 physchem columns and the aromatic-fraction column a weight of 4.0 and every fingerprint column a weight of 1.0. Set colsample_bynode=0.3 with colsample_bytree=1.0 so that each split draws its candidate features with probability proportional to these weights. This keeps the fingerprint diversity while making the physchem descriptors appear in more splits. Use DMatrix-level feature_weights with the same random_state=seed.

title: Snapshot averaging over boosting rounds
spec: Train the XGBoost L1 residual model once for 900 rounds at the incumbent learning_rate 0.03. Make predictions for the test set at three checkpoints, using the iteration_range argument of predict: rounds 400, 600 and 900 (iteration_range=(0,k)). Return the mean of the three predictions on the residual scale, added to the baseline. This is a free ensemble that smooths over the choice of the round count without extra training cost, and does not require inner validation.

title: Crippen atom-type contribution counts
spec: Keep the current pipeline. In featurize_one, use rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs(m) (or rdMolDescriptors.GetCrippenContribs) to get the Crippen logP atom type for each heavy atom. Count occurrences of each Crippen atom type across the train and test set vocabulary (build the vocabulary from training molecules only, keep unseen types dropped) and append these counts plus the summed Crippen logP and summed molar refractivity to the features. Use the same features for the physchem ridge base as an added 2-column input.

title: Multi-radius Morgan count features
spec: Replace the single radius-2 Morgan count vector with a multi-scale concatenation. Compute three count fingerprints with GetMorganGenerator: radius 1 with 1024 bits, radius 2 with 2048 bits (current), and radius 3 with 2048 bits, each hashed separately and each taken as counts. Concatenate them into one 5120-column block before the RDKit descriptors. Keep the two-stage XGBoost L1 model and the physchem ridge base unchanged. Set colsample_bytree to 0.2 to keep the per-tree feature budget similar to the current setting, because the input is now larger.

title: Pseudo-Huber objective in XGBoost
spec: In fit_predict, change the XGBRegressor objective from 'reg:absoluteerror' to 'reg:pseudohubererror' and set huber_slope to about 0.5 (the target is on a log scale, so residuals are mostly under 1). Keep every other setting, including the 600 rounds and learning_rate 0.03. The loss is still MAE, so the model is compared on the same metric. Use only the seed argument for randomness.

title: Monotone constraints on lipophilicity and polarity in XGBoost
spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost L1 pipeline. Build a monotone_constraints tuple of length equal to the feature count: 0 for every Morgan column and 0 for every RDKit descriptor column except MolLogP (+1) and TPSA (-1), located by their index in Descriptors.descList. Pass monotone_constraints to both XGBRegressor stages through params (tree_method='hist' already supports it). Physical intuition is that permeability rises with lipophilicity and falls with polar surface area, and the constraint regularizes the trees without changing the feature set.

title: Local weighted-median regression in physchem space
spec: Replace the global ridge physchem base with a local model. Standardize the 7 physchem features using training statistics. For each test molecule, take the k=60 nearest training molecules in that standardized space, with weights from a Gaussian kernel of distance (bandwidth set to the median neighbour distance). Fit a weighted linear regression with a small ridge penalty on those neighbours and predict the test value. Use this local prediction as base_te and base_tr (base_tr via leave-one-out neighbours) in place of the global Ridge base, and keep the XGBoost residual stages on top.

title: Descriptor-jitter augmentation for the residual booster
spec: Augment the stage-2 training set by stacking two copies of the training matrix. In the second copy, add Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.1 times the column standard deviation to the continuous RDKit descriptor columns only, and leave the fingerprint columns unchanged. Keep the labels and residuals as they are. Fit stage 2 on the stacked matrix (1456 rows) with reg:absoluteerror and the same learning rate and number of rounds, and keep the stage-1 model as before. The noise is a smoothing regularizer on the continuous descriptors, not on the labels.

title: Transductive physchem standardization
spec: Fit the StandardScaler used for the physchem base on the stacked train and test physchem matrices, not on train alone. This is unsupervised and uses only the SMILES, not labels. Keep the Ridge fit on train rows only, so the change affects only the scaling of the inputs. Also clip the standardized values of each physchem feature to the range [-4, 4] to limit the influence of outlier test molecules on the linear base. Everything else, including the two-stage XGBoost residual model, stays the same.

title: Gasteiger partial-charge surface descriptors
spec: Add charge-based descriptors to the feature vector. In featurize_one, call rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(m) and read the '_GasteigerCharge' property of each heavy atom, ignoring NaN values. Compute: maximum partial charge, minimum partial charge, sum of positive charges, sum of negative charges, the count of atoms with absolute charge above 0.25, and the charge-weighted surface proxy sum over heavy atoms of |charge| times the atom's TPSA contribution from rdMolDescriptors._CalcTPSAContribs. Append these six values to the feature vector and to the physchem ridge base input. Charges are computed per molecule, so there is no leakage.

title: Boosted-leaf kernel weighted median
spec: Keep the existing two-stage XGBoost residual model, but use it as a adaptive kernel. For each test molecule, find the leaf it lands in for every tree (booster.predict with pred_leaf=True). Weight each training molecule by the number of trees in which it shares a leaf with the test molecule, normalized. Predict the test value as base_te plus the weighted median of the training residuals (y minus base_tr), using the weights. This aligns the aggregation with the MAE objective instead of the mean of the leaf values. Use the same training data for the kernel as for the residuals.

title: Out-of-fold Tanimoto-kNN target feature for the boosted model
spec: Create one extra feature for the boosted stage: the Tanimoto-similarity-weighted mean of the training targets of each molecule's 10 nearest training neighbours. For the training rows, compute this out-of-fold with an inner 5-fold GroupKFold on Murcko scaffolds, so that a molecule never uses its own target or same-scaffold neighbours. For test rows, use all training molecules. Append the feature as one column to the XGBoost input for both stages. Use bit-vector Tanimoto from the Morgan bits.

title: Stage-one early stopping by inner scaffold holdout
spec: Choose the number of stage-1 squared-error rounds on the training data only, without touching the test fold. Split the training molecules into 4 groups by Murcko scaffold (GroupKFold on scaffold keys). Train the stage-1 model once for 400 rounds on three groups and record the validation MAE of the residual predictions at 50-round intervals, using the fold's training residuals. Pick the round count with the lowest validation MAE (restricted to 100 to 300 rounds), then refit the stage-1 model on all training data with that count and continue with the existing stage-2 L1 model unchanged.

title: Scaffold-grouped random search for stage-2 XGBoost settings
spec: Inside fit_predict, before the final fit, run a small random search (about 12 draws) over stage-2 XGBoost settings: max_depth in {3,4,5,6,8}, colsample_bytree in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5}, min_child_weight in {1,3,8}, learning_rate in {0.02,0.03,0.05}, and subsample in {0.6,0.8,1.0}. Score each draw by a 3-fold GroupKFold on train_smiles, grouping rows by Murcko scaffold, using MAE on the residual target y - base_tr. Refit the two-stage model (stage 1 squared error 200 rounds, stage 2 absolute error 400 rounds) with the best draw. Use seed for the sampler and the model. Keep the physchem ridge base unchanged.

title: Symbolic feature construction on physchem descriptors
spec: Before the physchem ridge, build a small set of nonlinear features from the physchem vector. Run a tiny genetic-programming search over expressions built from the 7 physchem columns (TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, aromatic fraction) using +, -, *, safe division, log1p(abs), and sqrt(abs). Use population 60 for 15 generations, with fitness equal to inner 3-fold GroupKFold MAE of a Ridge fit on the training rows, and keep the best 6 expressions. Append them to the standardized physchem features before the ridge base. Seed all random choices with seed.

title: Stage-two seed ensemble with column partitions
spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost residual model, but average the stage-2 predictions over 5 fits. Each fit uses seed+k for k in 0..4, and each fit restricts colsample to a different fixed random partition of the feature columns (half of the columns, drawn from rng(seed+k)). Average the five test predictions with equal weights. Do not change the stage-1 fit, which is shared. This is a cheap variance reduction on the stage-2 MAE fit.

title: Seed-diverse stage-two averaging with different column partitions
spec: Keep the stage-1 squared-error XGBoost model. Train three stage-2 L1 models starting from the same stage-1 booster, each with a different seed and a different random 50% partition of the columns made available to the model through feature_weights (set to 1 for the chosen columns and 0.2 for the rest). Average their residual predictions with the mean. The aim is to reduce variance from the column sampling without the cost of a full bagged ensemble. Keep the physchem ridge base and all other settings unchanged.

title: SMILES character n-gram TF-IDF features
spec: Keep the current physchem ridge base and two-stage XGBoost. Add a sparse feature block built from the raw canonical SMILES string: character n-grams with n in {2,3,4} (use a simple Python counter over substrings, no sklearn text vectorizer needed), keep only n-grams that occur in at least 5 training molecules, apply sublinear TF weighting and L2 row normalization, and scale to the scale of the other features. Append these columns to the Morgan-plus-descriptor matrix before both XGBoost stages. Fit the vocabulary on the training fold only; ignore unseen n-grams at test time.

title: Huber stage one with per-stage MAD scale
spec: Change only the stage-one objective. Replace reg:squarederror with reg:pseudohubererror and set huber_slope equal to 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the stage-one residual (y minus physchem base) on the training fold, computed once before fitting. Keep stage two (L1 absolute-error, 400 rounds, starting from the stage-one booster) and all other settings unchanged. This gives a robust start for the residual model that scales with the noise level of the training fold instead of relying on squared error.

title: Cauchy-loss IRLS physchem base
spec: Replace the Ridge physchem base with a robust linear fit solved by iteratively reweighted least squares. Start from the Ridge solution. At each of about 20 iterations, compute residuals on the training set, set a scale from the median absolute deviation (times 1.4826), and set weights w = 1/(1+(r/c)^2) with tuning constant c = 1.5 times that scale. Refit a weighted ridge (alpha=1.0) with those weights and stop when coefficients change by less than 1e-6. Use the fitted coefficients for base_tr and base_te, and keep the XGBoost residual stages unchanged.

title: Unhashed frequent-substructure count features
spec: Replace the hashed 2048-bit Morgan count vector with collision-free environment counts. Generate radius-1 to radius-3 Morgan environments with bitInfo (or the unfolded atom-environment identifiers) for each training molecule. Keep only environments that occur in at least 5 training molecules, and count them per molecule. Learn the kept vocabulary from the training fold only, and drop unseen environments at test time. Feed these columns, plus the existing descriptors, to the unchanged two-stage XGBoost residual model.

title: Robust median and IQR scaling for the physchem base
spec: In the physchem block, replace StandardScaler with robust scaling. Compute the column median and interquartile range from the training rows only, and divide by the IQR (fall back to 1 where the IQR is 0). Apply the same transform to the test rows. Keep Ridge(alpha=1.0) and the rest of the two-stage XGBoost residual model unchanged. This limits the influence of extreme MolWt and TPSA values on the linear base, which the current mean/SD scaling does not do.

title: Inner scaffold-group CV to choose the number of boosting rounds
spec: Split the training molecules into 4 folds using GroupKFold with Bemis-Murcko scaffold labels as groups, then train LightGBM with objective='l1' on each inner split with early stopping (patience 50, metric 'l1') to find the best iteration count. Average those best iteration counts and retrain on all training data with that many rounds. Tuning the stopping point on scaffold-held-out data matches the evaluation protocol.

title: Random-forest proximity-weighted median of residuals
spec: After the physchem Ridge base, fit a RandomForestRegressor (300 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=5, random_state=seed) on the log1p Morgan counts plus physchem features, with target y - base_tr. For each test molecule, compute the leaf co-membership weights against all training molecules (average over trees of 1/leaf-size for shared leaves), then predict base_te plus the weighted median of the training residuals under those weights (a quantile-regression-forest style estimate). This gives a nonparametric conditional-median residual correction, distinct from boosted-leaf kernels, and the L1 median suits the MAE metric.

title: Sparse Bayesian ARD linear base replacing physchem Ridge
spec: In fit_predict, replace the Ridge(alpha=1.0) physchem base with sklearn ARDRegression (default priors, max_iter=300) fit on the StandardScaler-transformed physchem features concatenated with the Morgan count columns that are nonzero in at least 5 training molecules (log1p-transformed). Use its predictions as base_tr and base_te exactly as the Ridge base is used now; the two XGBoost residual stages stay unchanged. Automatic relevance determination prunes weak fingerprint bits and gives a sparse Bayesian linear base, a family not yet tried for the base.

title: Supervised PLS components as extra features
spec: Before the XGBoost stages, fit sklearn PLSRegression (n_components=8) on the log1p Morgan count matrix against the training targets. To avoid leakage, produce the training-row PLS scores out-of-fold with an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) and fit a full-train PLS for the test rows. Append the 8 PLS score columns to the feature matrix of both XGBoost residual stages. Unlike the earlier truncated SVD, these components are target-supervised.

title: Laplace-likelihood natural-gradient booster (NGBoost-style)
spec: Replace the two-stage XGBoost residual model with a hand-written NGBoost-style booster that models the residual as Laplace(location mu, log-scale s). Initialize mu and s from the training residual median and log-MAD. For 300 rounds, compute the Laplace negative-log-likelihood gradients with respect to mu and s, rescale them by the inverse Fisher information (for Laplace, mu-scale 1/b^2 and s-scale 1 in the natural parametrization), fit a shallow XGBoost regressor (max_depth=4, 60 trees, learning_rate 0.1) to each natural gradient, and update mu and s with step 0.05. Predict the location mu for test molecules and add it to base_te. Optimizing the Laplace likelihood is the principled median-consistent objective, and natural-gradient steps are a family not tried yet.

title: Coarse histogram bins with per-node column sampling
spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost L1 model and features unchanged, but change the regularization of the tree building. Set max_bin=32 (coarser split candidates for the sparse count features) and colsample_bynode=0.5 in addition to the existing colsample_bytree=0.3, and keep all other parameters the same. The coarse bins and per-split feature sampling together act as a structural regularizer on the many sparse Morgan columns. Do not change the number of rounds.

title: Median-leaf gradient boosting with exact L1 leaf renewal
spec: Replace the stage-2 XGBoost call with a hand-written gradient-boosting loop on the residual target r = y - base_tr. Start from the median of r. In each of 300 rounds, compute the sign of the residual, fit a sklearn DecisionTreeRegressor (max_depth 5, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 3, random_state=seed) to the sign, and then reset each leaf value to the median of the actual residuals in that leaf. Add the tree to the prediction with shrinkage 0.05. Keep stage 1 as the squared-error XGBoost fit. Use this L1 learner for stage 2.

title: DART booster for dropout-style regularization
spec: Switch XGBoost to booster='dart' with rate_drop around 0.1, skip_drop around 0.5, and sample_type='uniform'. Keep reg:absoluteerror, max_depth 6, colsample_bytree 0.3, and subsample 0.8. Because DART is slower, raise the learning rate to about 0.05 and drop n_estimators to about 400. Predict with the default weights. Keep the seed argument as the only source of randomness.

title: Kernel ridge with RBF kernel as the physchem base
spec: Replace the linear Ridge physchem base with KernelRidge(kernel='rbf', alpha=1.0, gamma=1/7) on the standardized 7 physchem features, fit on the training rows only, with the target centered by the training mean before fitting and the mean added back at prediction time. The base predictions on the training rows are used to form the residuals for the two-stage XGBoost model, exactly as in the current script. This gives a nonlinear smooth base that captures the known curvature of permeability against TPSA without adding fingerprint noise.

title: Multi-output trees with auxiliary physchem targets
spec: In stage 1, fit one XGBoost model on a multi-target matrix: the main target (y - base_tr) plus the standardized values of TPSA, MolLogP, MolWt and NumHDonors, which are computed from training molecules only. Use tree_method='hist' with multi_strategy='multi_output_tree' (or the closest available multi-target option in the installed xgboost version; fall back to a single-target fit if it is unavailable). The auxiliary columns force shared splits that encode physicochemical structure into the trees. Use only the first output column as the residual prediction for test molecules. Stage 2 is the L1 model on the main target residual, unchanged.
